38	class BranchStore:
39	    """Named heads into a shared :class:`EventGraph`.
40	
41	    A branch is created from an existing event and grows only by appending
42	    events whose sole parent is the branch's current head, so branches
43	    never move each other's heads. Appends are idempotent: the store
44	    records the ``(at, changes)`` each branch appended under an event id,
45	    and repeating the same call is a no-op. All validation finishes before
46	    any state is touched, so a failed call leaves the graph, branch heads
47	    and idempotency records unchanged.
48	    """
49	
50	    #: Maximum number of live (unreleased) snapshot tokens per store.
51	    MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 32
52	
53	    def __init__(self, graph: EventGraph) -> None:
54	        if not isinstance(graph, EventGraph):
55	            raise TypeError(
56	                f"graph must be an EventGraph, got {type(graph).__name__}"
57	            )
58	        self._graph = graph
59	        self._heads: dict[str, str] = {}
60	        self._sources: dict[str, str] = {}
61	        self._appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = {}
62	        self._merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
63	        # token -> SnapshotEntry; only create_snapshot/release_snapshot and
64	        # the snapshot-aware lifetime queries touch it.
65	        self._snapshots: dict[str, "_SnapshotEntry"] = {}
66	        # Guards only the token registry and each entry's read accounting, so
67	        # a read reservation and the expiry decision stay one atomic step.
68	        self._snapshot_lock = threading.Lock()
69	        # Guards the mutable business state -- graph, heads, sources and the
70	        # append/merge records. create/append/merge run entirely under it and
71	        # checkpoint/snapshot capture copies under it, so a captured view can
72	        # never see the graph and records mid-commit.
73	        self._state_lock = threading.Lock()
74	
75	    @staticmethod
76	    def _require_nonempty_str(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
77	        # Same contract as EventGraph.add's string parameters.
78	        EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(value, name)
79	
80	    def _require_known_branch(self, name: str) -> None:
81	        if name not in self._heads:
82	            raise KeyError(name)
83	
84	    def create(self, name: str, from_event: str) -> None:
85	        """Create a branch named ``name`` starting at ``from_event``.
86	
87	        Re-creating with the same name and source is a no-op; the same
88	        name with a different source is a conflict.
89	        """
90	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
91	        self._require_nonempty_str(from_event, "from_event")
92	
93	        with self._state_lock:
94	            if name in self._heads:
95	                if self._sources[name] != from_event:
96	                    raise ValueError(
97	                        f"branch {name!r} already exists from "
98	                        f"{self._sources[name]!r}, not {from_event!r}"
99	                    )
100	                return
101	            if from_event not in self._graph._at:
102	                raise KeyError(from_event)
103	
104	            self._heads[name] = from_event
105	            self._sources[name] = from_event
106	            self._appends[name] = {}
107	
108	    def append(
109	        self,
110	        name: str,
111	        id: str,
112	        at: int,
113	        changes: dict[str, int],
114	    ) -> None:
115	        """Append an event whose sole parent is the branch's current head.
116	
117	        The head moves only if :meth:`EventGraph.add` succeeds. Repeating
118	        an append with the same ``name``/``id``/``at``/``changes`` is a
119	        no-op; reusing ``id`` with different inputs is a conflict, here
120	        and via the graph across branches.
121	        """
122	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
123	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
124	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
125	        # The at/changes contract is exactly EventGraph.add's.
126	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
127	        if at_value < 0:
128	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
129	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
130	            raise TypeError(
131	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
132	            )
133	        for key, value in changes.items():
134	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
135	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
136	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
137	        changes = dict(changes)
138	
139	        with self._state_lock:
140	            self._require_known_branch(name)
141	
142	            recorded = self._appends[name].get(id)
143	            if recorded is not None:
144	                if recorded == (at_value, changes):
145	                    return
146	                raise ValueError(
147	                    f"event {id!r} already appended on branch {name!r} "
148	                    f"with different inputs"
149	                )
150	
151	            head = self._heads[name]
152	            self._graph.add(id, at_value, (head,), changes)
153	
154	            # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
155	            self._heads[name] = id
156	            self._appends[name][id] = (at_value, changes)
157	
158	    def merge(
159	        self,
160	        target: str,
161	        source: str,
162	        id: str,
163	        at: int,
164	        changes: dict[str, int],
165	    ) -> None:
166	        """Merge ``source`` into ``target`` under a new two-parent event.
167	
168	        The event's parents are ordered ``(target head, source head)``;
169	        only the target head moves, the source head is untouched. Calls
170	        are idempotent on the exact five-tuple, and reusing ``id`` with
171	        different inputs (here or in the graph) is a conflict. A merge is
172	        rejected when events exclusive to either side touch overlapping
173	        change keys. All validation finishes before any state is touched,
174	        so a failed call leaves the graph, heads and records unchanged.
175	        """
176	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
177	        self._require_nonempty_str(target, "target")
178	        self._require_nonempty_str(source, "source")
179	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
180	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
181	        if at_value < 0:
182	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
183	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
184	            raise TypeError(
185	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
186	            )
187	        for key, value in changes.items():
188	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
189	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
190	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
191	        changes = dict(changes)
192	
193	        with self._state_lock:
194	            self._require_known_branch(target)
195	            self._require_known_branch(source)
196	            if target == source:
197	                raise ValueError(f"cannot merge branch {target!r} into itself")
198	
199	            recorded = self._merges.get(id)
200	            if recorded is not None:
201	                if recorded == (target, source, at_value, changes):
202	                    return
203	                raise ValueError(
204	                    f"merge event {id!r} already recorded with different inputs"
205	                )
206	
207	            target_head = self._heads[target]
208	            source_head = self._heads[source]
209	
210	            target_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(target_head))
211	            source_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(source_head))
212	            common = target_closure & source_closure
213	
214	            target_keys: set[str] = set()
215	            for event_id in target_closure - common:
216	                target_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
217	            source_keys: set[str] = set()
218	            for event_id in source_closure - common:
219	                source_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
220	            overlap = target_keys & source_keys
221	            if overlap:
222	                raise ValueError(
223	                    "conflicting changes on keys: "
224	                    + ", ".join(sorted(overlap))
225	                )
226	
227	            self._graph.add(id, at_value, (target_head, source_head), changes)
228	
229	            # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
230	            self._heads[target] = id
231	            self._merges[id] = (target, source, at_value, changes)
232	
233	    def create_snapshot(self, max_reads: int) -> str:
234	        """Freeze the current graph, heads and records into a snapshot token.
235	
236	        The token names a detached copy of everything the read-only
237	        lifetime queries consult: the full event graph (timestamps, parent
238	        tuples and per-event changes), every branch head, the append and
239	        merge records that form the audit log and idempotency keys. Later
240	        appends, merges or branch creation on this store never reach the
241	        token's view, and the snapshot never shares a mutable object with
242	        live state, so neither side can mutate the other.
243	
244	        ``max_reads`` must be a non-``bool`` :class:`int` (else
245	        :class:`TypeError`) of at least one (else :class:`ValueError`);
246	        it bounds how many token-bearing lifetime queries may succeed.
247	        At most :attr:`MAX_SNAPSHOTS` (32) unreleased tokens -- expired
248	        ones included -- may exist at once; reaching the cap raises
249	        :class:`RuntimeError` without evicting an older token or
250	        disturbing any existing one. Snapshot creation is read-only:
251	        success or failure never modifies the event graph, branch heads,
252	        audit or idempotency records.
253	        """
254	        if isinstance(max_reads, bool) or not isinstance(max_reads, int):
255	            raise TypeError(
256	                f"max_reads must be an int, got {type(max_reads).__name__}"
257	            )
258	        if max_reads < 1:
259	            raise ValueError("max_reads must be >= 1")
260	
261	        with self._snapshot_lock:
262	            # The cap is enforced before anything is copied, and expired
263	            # tokens are still unreleased, so they keep their slot until
264	            # release_snapshot frees it.
265	            if len(self._snapshots) >= self.MAX_SNAPSHOTS:
266	                raise RuntimeError(
267	                    f"snapshot token limit reached: at most "
268	                    f"{self.MAX_SNAPSHOTS} unreleased tokens per store"
269	                )
270	            with self._state_lock:
271	                state = self._snapshot_state()
272	            frozen = self._store_from_snapshot(state)
273	            while True:
274	                token = uuid.uuid4().hex
275	                if token not in self._snapshots:
276	                    break
277	            self._snapshots[token] = _SnapshotEntry(frozen, max_reads)
278	        return token
279	
280	    def release_snapshot(self, token: str) -> None:
281	        """Release a snapshot token, valid or expired, and free its slot.
282	
283	        ``token`` must be a non-empty :class:`str` (a non-``str`` raises
284	        :class:`TypeError`, an empty string :class:`ValueError`); an
285	        unknown token, one already released or one owned by another store
286	        raises :class:`KeyError`. Releasing a live token and releasing an
287	        expired token both succeed and return ``None``; the slot becomes
288	        reusable immediately and the token can never be restored. The
289	        release never modifies the event graph, branch heads, audit or
290	        idempotency records.
291	        """
292	        self._require_token_str(token)
293	        with self._snapshot_lock:
294	            entry = self._snapshots.pop(token, None)
295	        if entry is None:
296	            raise KeyError(token)
297	        return None
298	
299	    @staticmethod
300	    def _require_token_str(token: Any) -> None:
301	        """Validate the token parameter's type and emptiness."""
302	        if not isinstance(token, str):
303	            raise TypeError(
304	                f"token must be a str, got {type(token).__name__}"
305	            )
306	        if not token:
307	            raise ValueError("token must be a non-empty str")
308	
309	    def _reserve_snapshot_read(self, token: str) -> "BranchStore":
310	        """Validate ``token`` and atomically reserve one successful read.
311	
312	        Runs only after every ordinary query parameter has been validated.
313	        The type/emptiness checks precede the registry lookup: a non-``str``
314	        token raises :class:`TypeError`, an empty string raises
315	        :class:`ValueError`, and an unknown, released or foreign token
316	        raises :class:`KeyError`. A token whose allowance is exhausted is
317	        expired: the query raises :class:`RuntimeError` without consuming
318	        anything. Otherwise the allowance is decremented and the expiry
319	        decision is made in the same locked step, so at most ``max_reads``
320	        concurrent queries can ever succeed. Returns the token's frozen,
321	        detached :class:`BranchStore` view.
322	        """
323	        self._require_token_str(token)
324	        with self._snapshot_lock:
325	            entry = self._snapshots.get(token)
326	            if entry is None:
327	                raise KeyError(token)
328	            if entry.remaining <= 0:
329	                raise RuntimeError(
330	                    "snapshot token has expired: read allowance exhausted"
331	                )
332	            entry.remaining -= 1
333	            return entry.store
334	
335	    def _refund_snapshot_read(self, token: str) -> None:
336	        """Give a failed query's reserved read back to its token.
337	
338	        Query failures never consume the read allowance. A token released
339	        in the meantime has no entry left and needs no refund; an expired
340	        allowance restored here makes the token usable again, exactly as
341	        if the failing query had never run.
342	        """
343	        with self._snapshot_lock:
344	            entry = self._snapshots.get(token)
345	            if entry is not None:
346	                entry.remaining += 1

348	    def _snapshot_state(self) -> dict[str, object]:
349	        """Deep-copy the mutable business state as one consistent instant.
350	
351	        Must run while holding :attr:`_state_lock`, which serializes the
352	        copying against create/append/merge commits, so the event graph,
353	        branch heads and sources and the append/merge records can never be
354	        observed mid-commit. Every timestamp, parent tuple, change dict,
355	        head, source and record is copied; the result shares no mutable
356	        object with live state.
357	        """
358	        at: dict[str, int] = dict(self._graph._at)
359	        parents: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = dict(self._graph._parents)
360	        changes: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {
361	            event_id: dict(event_changes)
362	            for event_id, event_changes in self._graph._changes.items()
363	        }
364	        return {
365	            "at": at,
366	            "parents": parents,
367	            "changes": changes,
368	            "heads": dict(self._heads),
369	            "sources": dict(self._sources),
370	            "appends": {
371	                name: {
372	                    event_id: (at_value, dict(event_changes))
373	                    for event_id, (at_value, event_changes) in appends.items()
374	                }
375	                for name, appends in self._appends.items()
376	            },
377	            "merges": {
378	                event_id: (target, source, at_value, dict(event_changes))
379	                for event_id, (
380	                    target,
381	                    source,
382	                    at_value,
383	                    event_changes,
384	                ) in self._merges.items()
385	            },
386	        }

388	    @staticmethod
389	    def _store_from_snapshot(state: dict[str, object]) -> "BranchStore":
390	        """Build a detached store from a snapshot captured by
391	        :meth:`_snapshot_state` (or equivalent validated restore data).
392	
393	        The result shares no mutable object with ``state`` either, so
394	        later mutations of either side stay isolated.
395	        """
396	        graph = EventGraph()
397	        at = state["at"]
398	        parents = state["parents"]
399	        changes = state["changes"]
400	        for event_id in at:
401	            graph._at[event_id] = at[event_id]
402	            graph._parents[event_id] = tuple(parents[event_id])
403	            graph._changes[event_id] = dict(changes[event_id])
404	
405	        frozen = BranchStore(graph)
406	        frozen._heads = dict(state["heads"])
407	        frozen._sources = dict(state["sources"])
408	        frozen._appends = {
409	            name: {
410	                event_id: (at_value, dict(event_changes))
411	                for event_id, (at_value, event_changes) in appends.items()
412	            }
413	            for name, appends in state["appends"].items()
414	        }
415	        frozen._merges = {
416	            event_id: (target, source, at_value, dict(event_changes))
417	            for event_id, (
418	                target,
419	                source,
420	                at_value,
421	                event_changes,
422	            ) in state["merges"].items()
423	        }
424	        return frozen

430	    #: Checkpoint format version emitted by :meth:`save_checkpoint`.
431	    _CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 1
432	    _DOCUMENT_KEYS = ("schema_version", "payload", "checksum")
433	    _PAYLOAD_KEYS = ("events", "branches", "appends", "merges")
434	    _EVENT_KEYS = ("id", "at", "parents", "changes")
435	    _BRANCH_KEYS = ("name", "source", "head")
436	    _APPEND_RECORD_KEYS = ("at", "changes")
437	    _MERGE_RECORD_KEYS = ("target", "source", "at", "changes")
438	    _HEX_DIGITS = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")

440	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: Any) -> None:
441	        """Persist the store's business state to a versioned checkpoint file.
442	
443	        The file is UTF-8 (no BOM), compact JSON with no trailing newline;
444	        its top-level keys are ordered ``schema_version, payload,
445	        checksum`` with ``schema_version`` equal to 1. The payload stores,
446	        in order, the event graph, the branch table (source and head), and
447	        the append and merge idempotency/audit records. Event, branch and
448	        record identifiers and change keys are sorted by Unicode code
449	        point; parent ids keep their recorded order. The checksum is the
450	        lowercase hex SHA-256 of the payload's canonical JSON bytes. Equal
451	        business state always produces a byte-for-byte identical file.
452	
453	        ``path`` must be a non-empty :class:`str`: a non-``str`` raises
454	        :class:`TypeError` and an empty string :class:`ValueError`, both
455	        before any state is consulted. The state is copied as one
456	        consistent instant under the same lock that serializes
457	        create/append/merge, so concurrent mutations cannot leave the
458	        graph and records misaligned in the captured view, and neither
459	        success nor failure changes any business state; snapshot tokens,
460	        read allowances and release status are never persisted.
461	
462	        The bytes are written to a temporary file in the same directory,
463	        flushed and ``fsync``-ed, then atomically moved onto ``path``; if
464	        anything fails before the move, the previous target (if any) is
465	        left byte-for-byte untouched and the temporary file is removed.
466	        Open, read/write, flush or replace failures raise
467	        :class:`OSError`.
468	        """
469	        if not isinstance(path, str):
470	            raise TypeError(
471	                f"path must be a str, got {type(path).__name__}"
472	            )
473	        if not path:
474	            raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty str")
475	
476	        with self._state_lock:
477	            state = self._snapshot_state()
478	        payload = self._checkpoint_payload(state)
479	        payload_bytes = self._canonical_json(payload).encode("utf-8")
480	        checksum = hashlib.sha256(payload_bytes).hexdigest()
481	        document_bytes = self._canonical_json(
482	            {
483	                "schema_version": self._CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
484	                "payload": payload,
485	                "checksum": checksum,
486	            }
487	        ).encode("utf-8")
488	
489	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
490	        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
491	            prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory
492	        )
493	        replaced = False
494	        try:
495	            try:
496	                handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
497	            except BaseException:
498	                # fdopen only reaches here without taking ownership of fd.
499	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
500	                    os.close(fd)
501	                raise
502	            with handle:
503	                handle.write(document_bytes)
504	                handle.flush()
505	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
506	            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
507	            replaced = True
508	        finally:
509	            if not replaced:
510	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
511	                    os.remove(tmp_path)
512	        return None
513	
514	    @classmethod
515	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: Any) -> "BranchStore":
516	        """Restore a :class:`BranchStore` from a file written by
517	        :meth:`save_checkpoint`.
518	
519	        ``path`` must be a non-empty :class:`str`: a non-``str`` raises
520	        :class:`TypeError` and an empty string :class:`ValueError`, both
521	        before the file is opened; filesystem failures (missing file,
522	        permissions, read errors) propagate as :class:`OSError`. Every
523	        other defect -- invalid UTF-8 or BOM, malformed JSON, wrong
524	        top-level shape, a missing/extra field, a wrong type, an empty
525	        identifier, a ``bool`` posing as an integer, a negative
526	        timestamp, an unsupported :class:`schema_version`, a checksum
527	        mismatch, duplicate events or parents, unknown parents, cycles,
528	        unknown branch heads or sources, append/merge records that do not
529	        match the events, parent order or branch lineage -- raises
530	        :class:`ValueError`. The checksum is verified against the
531	        payload before any object is built.
532	
533	        On failure nothing partial is returned and the file is never
534	        modified; on success the returned store is a fresh instance whose
535	        replay, audit, conflict and idempotency behavior is identical to
536	        the saved one, but which shares no mutable state with the saved
537	        instance or the parsed JSON. Snapshot tokens are not persisted,
538	        so the restored store's token table is always empty and its read
539	        allowances start fresh.
540	        """
541	        if not isinstance(path, str):
542	            raise TypeError(
543	                f"path must be a str, got {type(path).__name__}"
544	            )
545	        if not path:
546	            raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty str")
547	
548	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
549	            raw = handle.read()
550	
551	        if raw.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
552	            raise ValueError("checkpoint must be UTF-8 without a BOM")
553	        try:
554	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
555	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
556	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid UTF-8: {exc}") from exc
557	        # The hook raises ValueError (not JSONDecodeError) on duplicate keys;
558	        # it propagates directly, so both parse failures are ValueError.
559	        try:
560	            document = json.loads(
561	                text, object_pairs_hook=cls._reject_duplicate_json_keys
562	            )
563	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
564	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
565	
566	        state = cls._parse_checkpoint_document(document)
567	        return cls._store_from_snapshot(state)
568	
569	    @staticmethod
570	    def _canonical_json(value: Any) -> str:
571	        """Compact, deterministic JSON: no whitespace, non-ASCII literal,
572	        no non-finite floats and no trailing newline."""
573	        return json.dumps(
574	            value,
575	            separators=(",", ":"),
576	            ensure_ascii=False,
577	            allow_nan=False,
578	        )
579	
580	    @staticmethod
581	    def _reject_duplicate_json_keys(
582	        pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]],
583	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
584	        """``object_pairs_hook`` treating duplicate JSON keys as invalid."""
585	        result: dict[str, Any] = {}
586	        for key, value in pairs:
587	            if key in result:
588	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate key {key!r} in JSON object")
589	            result[key] = value
590	        return result

"""Named branches over a shared event graph."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import hashlib
import heapq
import hmac
import itertools
import json
import math
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import uuid
from typing import Any

from city_twin.event_graph import EventGraph


class _SnapshotEntry:
    """One snapshot token's frozen view and remaining read allowance.

    ``store`` is a detached :class:`BranchStore` holding deep copies of the
    creating store's event graph, heads and records at creation time; it is
    never mutated afterwards. ``remaining`` counts successful queries only
    and reaches zero exactly when the token expires. Read accounting and
    expiry are decided under the owning store's snapshot lock.
    """

    __slots__ = ("store", "remaining")

    def __init__(self, store: "BranchStore", max_reads: int) -> None:
        self.store = store
        self.remaining = max_reads


class BranchStore:
    """Named heads into a shared :class:`EventGraph`.

    A branch is created from an existing event and grows only by appending
    events whose sole parent is the branch's current head, so branches
    never move each other's heads. Appends are idempotent: the store
    records the ``(at, changes)`` each branch appended under an event id,
    and repeating the same call is a no-op. All validation finishes before
    any state is touched, so a failed call leaves the graph, branch heads
    and idempotency records unchanged.
    """

    #: Maximum number of live (unreleased) snapshot tokens per store.
    MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 32

    def __init__(self, graph: EventGraph) -> None:
        if not isinstance(graph, EventGraph):
            raise TypeError(
                f"graph must be an EventGraph, got {type(graph).__name__}"
            )
        self._graph = graph
        self._heads: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._sources: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = {}
        self._merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
        # token -> SnapshotEntry; only create_snapshot/release_snapshot and
        # the snapshot-aware lifetime queries touch it.
        self._snapshots: dict[str, "_SnapshotEntry"] = {}
        # Guards only the token registry and each entry's read accounting, so
        # a read reservation and the expiry decision stay one atomic step.
        self._snapshot_lock = threading.Lock()
        # Guards the mutable business state -- graph, heads, sources and the
        # append/merge records. create/append/merge run entirely under it and
        # checkpoint/snapshot capture copies under it, so a captured view can
        # never see the graph and records mid-commit.
        self._state_lock = threading.Lock()

    @staticmethod
    def _require_nonempty_str(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
        # Same contract as EventGraph.add's string parameters.
        EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(value, name)

    def _require_known_branch(self, name: str) -> None:
        if name not in self._heads:
            raise KeyError(name)

    def create(self, name: str, from_event: str) -> None:
        """Create a branch named ``name`` starting at ``from_event``.

        Re-creating with the same name and source is a no-op; the same
        name with a different source is a conflict.
        """
        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
        self._require_nonempty_str(from_event, "from_event")

        with self._state_lock:
            if name in self._heads:
                if self._sources[name] != from_event:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"branch {name!r} already exists from "
                        f"{self._sources[name]!r}, not {from_event!r}"
                    )
                return
            if from_event not in self._graph._at:
                raise KeyError(from_event)

            self._heads[name] = from_event
            self._sources[name] = from_event
            self._appends[name] = {}

    def append(
        self,
        name: str,
        id: str,
        at: int,
        changes: dict[str, int],
    ) -> None:
        """Append an event whose sole parent is the branch's current head.

        The head moves only if :meth:`EventGraph.add` succeeds. Repeating
        an append with the same ``name``/``id``/``at``/``changes`` is a
        no-op; reusing ``id`` with different inputs is a conflict, here
        and via the graph across branches.
        """
        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
        # The at/changes contract is exactly EventGraph.add's.
        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
        if at_value < 0:
            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
            raise TypeError(
                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
            )
        for key, value in changes.items():
            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
        changes = dict(changes)

        with self._state_lock:
            self._require_known_branch(name)

            recorded = self._appends[name].get(id)
            if recorded is not None:
                if recorded == (at_value, changes):
                    return
                raise ValueError(
                    f"event {id!r} already appended on branch {name!r} "
                    f"with different inputs"
                )

            head = self._heads[name]
            self._graph.add(id, at_value, (head,), changes)

            # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
            self._heads[name] = id
            self._appends[name][id] = (at_value, changes)

    def merge(
        self,
        target: str,
        source: str,
        id: str,
        at: int,
        changes: dict[str, int],
    ) -> None:
        """Merge ``source`` into ``target`` under a new two-parent event.

        The event's parents are ordered ``(target head, source head)``;
        only the target head moves, the source head is untouched. Calls
        are idempotent on the exact five-tuple, and reusing ``id`` with
        different inputs (here or in the graph) is a conflict. A merge is
        rejected when events exclusive to either side touch overlapping
        change keys. All validation finishes before any state is touched,
        so a failed call leaves the graph, heads and records unchanged.
        """
        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
        self._require_nonempty_str(target, "target")
        self._require_nonempty_str(source, "source")
        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
        if at_value < 0:
            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
            raise TypeError(
                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
            )
        for key, value in changes.items():
            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
        changes = dict(changes)

        with self._state_lock:
            self._require_known_branch(target)
            self._require_known_branch(source)
            if target == source:
                raise ValueError(f"cannot merge branch {target!r} into itself")

            recorded = self._merges.get(id)
            if recorded is not None:
                if recorded == (target, source, at_value, changes):
                    return
                raise ValueError(
                    f"merge event {id!r} already recorded with different inputs"
                )

            target_head = self._heads[target]
            source_head = self._heads[source]

            target_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(target_head))
            source_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(source_head))
            common = target_closure & source_closure

            target_keys: set[str] = set()
            for event_id in target_closure - common:
                target_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
            source_keys: set[str] = set()
            for event_id in source_closure - common:
                source_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
            overlap = target_keys & source_keys
            if overlap:
                raise ValueError(
                    "conflicting changes on keys: "
                    + ", ".join(sorted(overlap))
                )

            self._graph.add(id, at_value, (target_head, source_head), changes)

            # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
            self._heads[target] = id
            self._merges[id] = (target, source, at_value, changes)

    def create_snapshot(self, max_reads: int) -> str:
        """Freeze the current graph, heads and records into a snapshot token.

        The token names a detached copy of everything the read-only
        lifetime queries consult: the full event graph (timestamps, parent
        tuples and per-event changes), every branch head, the append and
        merge records that form the audit log and idempotency keys. Later
        appends, merges or branch creation on this store never reach the
        token's view, and the snapshot never shares a mutable object with
        live state, so neither side can mutate the other.

        ``max_reads`` must be a non-``bool`` :class:`int` (else
        :class:`TypeError`) of at least one (else :class:`ValueError`);
        it bounds how many token-bearing lifetime queries may succeed.
        At most :attr:`MAX_SNAPSHOTS` (32) unreleased tokens -- expired
        ones included -- may exist at once; reaching the cap raises
        :class:`RuntimeError` without evicting an older token or
        disturbing any existing one. Snapshot creation is read-only:
        success or failure never modifies the event graph, branch heads,
        audit or idempotency records.
        """
        if isinstance(max_reads, bool) or not isinstance(max_reads, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"max_reads must be an int, got {type(max_reads).__name__}"
            )
        if max_reads < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_reads must be >= 1")

        with self._snapshot_lock:
            # The cap is enforced before anything is copied, and expired
            # tokens are still unreleased, so they keep their slot until
            # release_snapshot frees it.
            if len(self._snapshots) >= self.MAX_SNAPSHOTS:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"snapshot token limit reached: at most "
                    f"{self.MAX_SNAPSHOTS} unreleased tokens per store"
                )
            with self._state_lock:
                state = self._snapshot_state()
            frozen = self._store_from_snapshot(state)
            while True:
                token = uuid.uuid4().hex
                if token not in self._snapshots:
                    break
            self._snapshots[token] = _SnapshotEntry(frozen, max_reads)
        return token

    def release_snapshot(self, token: str) -> None:
        """Release a snapshot token, valid or expired, and free its slot.

        ``token`` must be a non-empty :class:`str` (a non-``str`` raises
        :class:`TypeError`, an empty string :class:`ValueError`); an
        unknown token, one already released or one owned by another store
        raises :class:`KeyError`. Releasing a live token and releasing an
        expired token both succeed and return ``None``; the slot becomes
        reusable immediately and the token can never be restored. The
        release never modifies the event graph, branch heads, audit or
        idempotency records.
        """
        self._require_token_str(token)
        with self._snapshot_lock:
            entry = self._snapshots.pop(token, None)
        if entry is None:
            raise KeyError(token)
        return None

    @staticmethod
    def _require_token_str(token: Any) -> None:
        """Validate the token parameter's type and emptiness."""
        if not isinstance(token, str):
            raise TypeError(
                f"token must be a str, got {type(token).__name__}"
            )
        if not token:
            raise ValueError("token must be a non-empty str")

    def _reserve_snapshot_read(self, token: str) -> "BranchStore":
        """Validate ``token`` and atomically reserve one successful read.

        Runs only after every ordinary query parameter has been validated.
        The type/emptiness checks precede the registry lookup: a non-``str``
        token raises :class:`TypeError`, an empty string raises
        :class:`ValueError`, and an unknown, released or foreign token
        raises :class:`KeyError`. A token whose allowance is exhausted is
        expired: the query raises :class:`RuntimeError` without consuming
        anything. Otherwise the allowance is decremented and the expiry
        decision is made in the same locked step, so at most ``max_reads``
        concurrent queries can ever succeed. Returns the token's frozen,
        detached :class:`BranchStore` view.
        """
        self._require_token_str(token)
        with self._snapshot_lock:
            entry = self._snapshots.get(token)
            if entry is None:
                raise KeyError(token)
            if entry.remaining <= 0:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "snapshot token has expired: read allowance exhausted"
                )
            entry.remaining -= 1
            return entry.store

    def _refund_snapshot_read(self, token: str) -> None:
        """Give a failed query's reserved read back to its token.

        Query failures never consume the read allowance. A token released
        in the meantime has no entry left and needs no refund; an expired
        allowance restored here makes the token usable again, exactly as
        if the failing query had never run.
        """
        with self._snapshot_lock:
            entry = self._snapshots.get(token)
            if entry is not None:
                entry.remaining += 1

    def _snapshot_state(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Deep-copy the mutable business state as one consistent instant.

        Must run while holding :attr:`_state_lock`, which serializes the
        copying against create/append/merge commits, so the event graph,
        branch heads and sources and the append/merge records can never be
        observed mid-commit. Every timestamp, parent tuple, change dict,
        head, source and record is copied; the result shares no mutable
        object with live state.
        """
        at: dict[str, int] = dict(self._graph._at)
        parents: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = dict(self._graph._parents)
        changes: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {
            event_id: dict(event_changes)
            for event_id, event_changes in self._graph._changes.items()
        }
        return {
            "at": at,
            "parents": parents,
            "changes": changes,
            "heads": dict(self._heads),
            "sources": dict(self._sources),
            "appends": {
                name: {
                    event_id: (at_value, dict(event_changes))
                    for event_id, (at_value, event_changes) in appends.items()
                }
                for name, appends in self._appends.items()
            },
            "merges": {
                event_id: (target, source, at_value, dict(event_changes))
                for event_id, (
                    target,
                    source,
                    at_value,
                    event_changes,
                ) in self._merges.items()
            },
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _store_from_snapshot(state: dict[str, object]) -> "BranchStore":
        """Build a detached store from a snapshot captured by
        :meth:`_snapshot_state` (or equivalent validated restore data).

        The result shares no mutable object with ``state`` either, so
        later mutations of either side stay isolated.
        """
        graph = EventGraph()
        at = state["at"]
        parents = state["parents"]
        changes = state["changes"]
        for event_id in at:
            graph._at[event_id] = at[event_id]
            graph._parents[event_id] = tuple(parents[event_id])
            graph._changes[event_id] = dict(changes[event_id])

        frozen = BranchStore(graph)
        frozen._heads = dict(state["heads"])
        frozen._sources = dict(state["sources"])
        frozen._appends = {
            name: {
                event_id: (at_value, dict(event_changes))
                for event_id, (at_value, event_changes) in appends.items()
            }
            for name, appends in state["appends"].items()
        }
        frozen._merges = {
            event_id: (target, source, at_value, dict(event_changes))
            for event_id, (
                target,
                source,
                at_value,
                event_changes,
            ) in state["merges"].items()
        }
        return frozen

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Versioned, checksummed persistence
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    #: Checkpoint format version emitted by :meth:`save_checkpoint`.
    _CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 1
    _DOCUMENT_KEYS = ("schema_version", "payload", "checksum")
    _PAYLOAD_KEYS = ("events", "branches", "appends", "merges")
    _EVENT_KEYS = ("id", "at", "parents", "changes")
    _BRANCH_KEYS = ("name", "source", "head")
    _APPEND_RECORD_KEYS = ("at", "changes")
    _MERGE_RECORD_KEYS = ("target", "source", "at", "changes")
    _HEX_DIGITS = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")

    def save_checkpoint(self, path: Any) -> None:
        """Persist the store's business state to a versioned checkpoint file.

        The file is UTF-8 (no BOM), compact JSON with no trailing newline;
        its top-level keys are ordered ``schema_version, payload,
        checksum`` with ``schema_version`` equal to 1. The payload stores,
        in order, the event graph, the branch table (source and head), and
        the append and merge idempotency/audit records. Event, branch and
        record identifiers and change keys are sorted by Unicode code
        point; parent ids keep their recorded order. The checksum is the
        lowercase hex SHA-256 of the payload's canonical JSON bytes. Equal
        business state always produces a byte-for-byte identical file.

        ``path`` must be a non-empty :class:`str`: a non-``str`` raises
        :class:`TypeError` and an empty string :class:`ValueError`, both
        before any state is consulted. The state is copied as one
        consistent instant under the same lock that serializes
        create/append/merge, so concurrent mutations cannot leave the
        graph and records misaligned in the captured view, and neither
        success nor failure changes any business state; snapshot tokens,
        read allowances and release status are never persisted.

        The bytes are written to a temporary file in the same directory,
        flushed and ``fsync``-ed, then atomically moved onto ``path``; if
        anything fails before the move, the previous target (if any) is
        left byte-for-byte untouched and the temporary file is removed.
        Open, read/write, flush or replace failures raise
        :class:`OSError`.
        """
        if not isinstance(path, str):
            raise TypeError(
                f"path must be a str, got {type(path).__name__}"
            )
        if not path:
            raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty str")

        with self._state_lock:
            state = self._snapshot_state()
        payload = self._checkpoint_payload(state)
        payload_bytes = self._canonical_json(payload).encode("utf-8")
        checksum = hashlib.sha256(payload_bytes).hexdigest()
        document_bytes = self._canonical_json(
            {
                "schema_version": self._CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
                "payload": payload,
                "checksum": checksum,
            }
        ).encode("utf-8")

        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
            prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory
        )
        replaced = False
        try:
            try:
                handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
            except BaseException:
                # fdopen only reaches here without taking ownership of fd.
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.close(fd)
                raise
            with handle:
                handle.write(document_bytes)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
            replaced = True
        finally:
            if not replaced:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(tmp_path)
        return None

    @classmethod
    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: Any) -> "BranchStore":
        """Restore a :class:`BranchStore` from a file written by
        :meth:`save_checkpoint`.

        ``path`` must be a non-empty :class:`str`: a non-``str`` raises

        before the file is opened; filesystem failures (missing file,
        permissions, read errors) propagate as :class:`OSError`. Every
        other defect -- invalid UTF-8 or BOM, malformed JSON, wrong
        top-level shape, a missing/extra field, a wrong type, an empty
        identifier, a ``bool`` posing as an integer, a negative
        timestamp, an unsupported :class:`schema_version`, a checksum
        mismatch, duplicate events or parents, unknown parents, cycles,
        unknown branch heads or sources, append/merge records that do not
        match the events, parent order or branch lineage -- raises
        :class:`ValueError`. The checksum is verified against the
        payload before any object is built.

        On failure nothing partial is returned and the file is never
        modified; on success the returned store is a fresh instance whose
        replay, audit, conflict and idempotency behavior is identical to
        the saved one, but which shares no mutable state with the saved
        instance or the parsed JSON. Snapshot tokens are not persisted,
        so the restored store's token table is always empty and its read
        allowances start fresh.
        """
        if not isinstance(path, str):

        return cls._store_from_snapshot(state)

    @staticmethod

            separators=(",", ":"),
            ensure_ascii=False,
            allow_nan=False,

664	    @classmethod
665	    def _parse_checkpoint_document(cls, document: Any) -> dict[str, object]:
666	        """Validate the envelope, verify the checksum, parse and validate
667	        the payload into fresh local structures."""
668	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
669	            raise ValueError("top-level JSON value must be an object")
670	        if set(document.keys()) != set(cls._DOCUMENT_KEYS):
671	            raise ValueError(
672	                "top-level object must contain exactly the keys "
673	                "'schema_version', 'payload' and 'checksum'"
674	            )
675	
676	        version = document["schema_version"]
677	        if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
678	            raise ValueError("'schema_version' must be an int")
679	        if version != cls._CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
680	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported schema_version {version!r}")
681	
682	        checksum = document["checksum"]
683	        if not isinstance(checksum, str) or len(checksum) != 64 or (
684	            set(checksum) - cls._HEX_DIGITS
685	        ):
686	            raise ValueError(
687	                "'checksum' must be a 64-character lowercase hex string"
688	            )
689	
690	        payload = document["payload"]
691	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
692	            raise ValueError("'payload' must be an object")
693	        if set(payload.keys()) != set(cls._PAYLOAD_KEYS):
694	            raise ValueError(
695	                "payload must contain exactly the keys 'events', "
696	                "'branches', 'appends' and 'merges'"
697	            )
698	
699	        # Re-serializing the parsed payload reproduces the writer's
700	        # canonical bytes; the checksum must match before anything is built.
701	        try:
702	            payload_text = cls._canonical_json(payload)
703	        except ValueError as exc:
704	            raise ValueError(f"payload is not canonicalizable JSON: {exc}")
705	        actual = hashlib.sha256(payload_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
706	        if not hmac.compare_digest(actual, checksum):
707	            raise ValueError("checksum does not match payload")
708	
709	        state = cls._parse_checkpoint_payload(payload)
710	        cls._validate_checkpoint_state(state)
711	        return state

713	    @classmethod
714	    def _parse_checkpoint_payload(cls, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, object]:
715	        """Strict structural parse of the payload into local state."""
716	        raw_events = payload["events"]
717	        if not isinstance(raw_events, list):
718	            raise ValueError("'events' must be an array")
719	
720	        at_values: dict[str, int] = {}
721	        parent_map: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
722	        change_map: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
723	        for index, event in enumerate(raw_events):
724	            if not isinstance(event, dict):
725	                raise ValueError(f"event at index {index} must be an object")
726	            if set(event.keys()) != set(cls._EVENT_KEYS):
727	                raise ValueError(
728	                    f"event at index {index} must contain exactly the keys "
729	                    "'id', 'at', 'parents' and 'changes'"
730	                )
731	            event_id = event["id"]
732	            if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not event_id:
733	                raise ValueError(
734	                    f"event at index {index}: id must be a non-empty str"
735	                )
736	            if event_id in at_values:
737	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate event id {event_id!r}")
738	            at_value = event["at"]
739	            if isinstance(at_value, bool) or not isinstance(at_value, int):
740	                raise ValueError(f"event {event_id!r}: at must be an int")
741	            if at_value < 0:
742	                raise ValueError(f"event {event_id!r}: at must be non-negative")
743	            raw_parents = event["parents"]
744	            if not isinstance(raw_parents, list):
745	                raise ValueError(f"event {event_id!r}: parents must be an array")
746	            event_parents: list[str] = []
747	            seen_parents: set[str] = set()
748	            for parent in raw_parents:
749	                if not isinstance(parent, str) or not parent:
750	                    raise ValueError(
751	                        f"event {event_id!r}: every parent must be a "
752	                        "non-empty str"
753	                    )
754	                if parent in seen_parents:
755	                    raise ValueError(
756	                        f"event {event_id!r}: duplicate parent {parent!r}"
757	                    )
758	                seen_parents.add(parent)
759	                event_parents.append(parent)
760	            event_changes = cls._parse_change_object(
761	                event["changes"], f"event {event_id!r}"
762	            )
763	            at_values[event_id] = at_value
764	            parent_map[event_id] = tuple(event_parents)
765	            change_map[event_id] = event_changes
766	
767	        raw_branches = payload["branches"]
768	        if not isinstance(raw_branches, list):
769	            raise ValueError("'branches' must be an array")
770	        heads: dict[str, str] = {}
771	        sources: dict[str, str] = {}
772	        for index, branch in enumerate(raw_branches):
773	            if not isinstance(branch, dict):
774	                raise ValueError(f"branch at index {index} must be an object")
775	            if set(branch.keys()) != set(cls._BRANCH_KEYS):
776	                raise ValueError(
777	                    f"branch at index {index} must contain exactly the keys "
778	                    "'name', 'source' and 'head'"
779	                )
780	            name = branch["name"]
781	            source = branch["source"]
782	            head = branch["head"]
783	            for label, value in (
784	                ("name", name),
785	                ("source", source),
786	                ("head", head),
787	            ):
788	                if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
789	                    raise ValueError(
790	                        f"branch at index {index}: {label} must be a "
791	                        "non-empty str"
792	                    )
793	            if name in heads:
794	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate branch name {name!r}")
795	            heads[name] = head
796	            sources[name] = source
797	
798	        raw_appends = payload["appends"]
799	        if not isinstance(raw_appends, dict):
800	            raise ValueError("'appends' must be an object")
801	        appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = {}
802	        for name, raw_records in raw_appends.items():
803	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
804	                raise ValueError("every appends group key must be a non-empty str")
805	            if not isinstance(raw_records, dict):
806	                raise ValueError(
807	                    f"append records for branch {name!r} must be an object"
808	                )
809	            branch_appends: dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
810	            for event_id, record in raw_records.items():
811	                if not event_id:
812	                    raise ValueError(
813	                        f"branch {name!r}: append event id must be a non-empty str"
814	                    )
815	                at_value, event_changes = cls._parse_record(
816	                    record,
817	                    cls._APPEND_RECORD_KEYS,
818	                    f"append record {event_id!r}",
819	                )
820	                if event_id in branch_appends:
821	                    raise ValueError(
822	                        f"duplicate append record for event {event_id!r} "
823	                        f"on branch {name!r}"
824	                    )
825	                branch_appends[event_id] = (at_value, event_changes)

827	
828	        raw_merges = payload["merges"]
829	        if not isinstance(raw_merges, dict):
830	            raise ValueError("'merges' must be an object")
831	        merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
832	        for event_id, record in raw_merges.items():
833	            if not event_id:
834	                raise ValueError("merge event id must be a non-empty str")
835	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
836	                raise ValueError(f"merge record {event_id!r} must be an object")
837	            if set(record.keys()) != set(cls._MERGE_RECORD_KEYS):
838	                raise ValueError(
839	                    f"merge record {event_id!r} must contain exactly the keys "
840	                    "'target', 'source', 'at' and 'changes'"
841	                )
842	            target = record["target"]
843	            source = record["source"]
844	            if not isinstance(target, str) or not target:
845	                raise ValueError(
846	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: target must be a non-empty str"
847	                )
848	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
849	                raise ValueError(
850	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: source must be a non-empty str"
851	                )
852	            at_value = record["at"]
853	            if isinstance(at_value, bool) or not isinstance(at_value, int):
854	                raise ValueError(f"merge record {event_id!r}: at must be an int")
855	            if at_value < 0:
856	                raise ValueError(
857	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: at must be non-negative"
858	                )
859	            event_changes = cls._parse_change_object(
860	                record["changes"], f"merge record {event_id!r}"
861	            )
862	            if event_id in merges:
863	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate merge record for event {event_id!r}")
864	            merges[event_id] = (target, source, at_value, event_changes)
865	
866	        return {
867	            "at": at_values,
868	            "parents": parent_map,
869	            "changes": change_map,
870	            "heads": heads,
871	            "sources": sources,
872	            "appends": appends,
873	            "merges": merges,
874	        }

876	    @classmethod
877	    def _parse_record(
878	        cls, record: Any, expected_keys: tuple[str, ...], label: str
879	    ) -> tuple[int, dict[str, int]]:
880	        """Parse an ``{"at", "changes"}`` style record object."""
881	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
882	            raise ValueError(f"{label} must be an object")
883	        if set(record.keys()) != set(expected_keys):
884	            raise ValueError(f"{label} has an unexpected set of keys")
885	        at_value = record["at"]
886	        if isinstance(at_value, bool) or not isinstance(at_value, int):
887	            raise ValueError(f"{label}: at must be an int")
888	        if at_value < 0:
889	            raise ValueError(f"{label}: at must be non-negative")

892	    @staticmethod
893	    def _parse_change_object(raw: Any, label: str) -> dict[str, int]:
894	        """Parse and copy a ``{non-empty str: int-not-bool}`` object."""
895	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
896	            raise ValueError(f"{label}: changes must be an object")
897	        event_changes: dict[str, int] = {}
898	        for key, value in raw.items():
899	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
900	                raise ValueError(
901	                    f"{label}: every change key must be a non-empty str"
902	                )
903	            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
904	                raise ValueError(
905	                    f"{label}: change value for {key!r} must be an int"
906	                )
907	            event_changes[key] = value
908	        return event_changes

910	    @classmethod
911	    def _validate_checkpoint_state(cls, state: dict[str, object]) -> None:
912	        """Cross-field validation: graph integrity, branch lineage and
913	        record/event agreement. Raises ValueError on the first defect."""
914	        at_values: dict[str, int] = state["at"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
915	        parent_map: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = state["parents"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
916	        change_map: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = state["changes"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
917	        heads: dict[str, str] = state["heads"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
918	        sources: dict[str, str] = state["sources"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
919	        appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = state[  # type: ignore[assignment]
920	            "appends"
921	        ]
922	        merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = state[  # type: ignore[assignment]
923	            "merges"
924	        ]
925	
926	        # Append/merge records may only be grouped under known branches and
927	        # an event is recorded at most once across all records.
928	        recorded_events: set[str] = set()
929	        for name, branch_appends in appends.items():
930	            if name not in heads:
931	                raise ValueError(f"append record for unknown branch {name!r}")
932	            for event_id in branch_appends:
933	                if event_id in recorded_events:
934	                    raise ValueError(
935	                        f"event {event_id!r} is recorded more than once"
936	                    )
937	                recorded_events.add(event_id)
938	        for event_id, (target, source, _, _) in merges.items():
939	            if target not in heads:
940	                raise ValueError(
941	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: unknown target branch "
942	                    f"{target!r}"
943	                )
944	            if source not in heads:
945	                raise ValueError(
946	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: unknown source branch "
947	                    f"{source!r}"
948	                )
949	            if target == source:
950	                raise ValueError(
951	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: target and source must "
952	                    "differ"
953	                )
954	            if event_id in recorded_events:
955	                raise ValueError(
956	                    f"event {event_id!r} is recorded more than once"
957	                )
958	            recorded_events.add(event_id)
959	
960	        # Graph: every parent is known.
961	        for event_id, event_parents in parent_map.items():
962	            for parent in event_parents:
963	                if parent not in at_values:
964	                    raise ValueError(
965	                        f"event {event_id!r}: unknown parent {parent!r}"
966	                    )
967	
968	        # Graph: cycle detection via iterative child -> parent DFS.
969	        white, gray, black = 0, 1, 2
970	        color = {event_id: white for event_id in at_values}
971	        for start in at_values:
972	            if color[start] != white:
973	                continue
974	            color[start] = gray
975	            stack: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(start, 0)]
976	            while stack:
977	                node, cursor = stack[-1]
978	                node_parents = parent_map[node]
979	                if cursor < len(node_parents):
980	                    nxt = node_parents[cursor]
981	                    stack[-1] = (node, cursor + 1)
982	                    if color[nxt] == gray:
983	                        raise ValueError(
984	                            f"cycle detected involving event {nxt!r}"
985	                        )
986	                    if color[nxt] == white:
987	                        color[nxt] = gray
988	                        stack.append((nxt, 0))
989	                else:
990	                    color[node] = black
991	                    stack.pop()
992	
993	        # Recorded events must agree with graph events, timestamps, changes
994	        # and parent arity.
995	        for name, branch_appends in appends.items():
996	            for event_id, (recorded_at, recorded_changes) in (
997	                branch_appends.items()
998	            ):
999	                if event_id not in at_values:
1000	                    raise ValueError(
1001	                        f"append record {event_id!r} on branch {name!r} "
1002	                        "has no matching event"
1003	                    )
1004	                if at_values[event_id] != recorded_at:
1005	                    raise ValueError(
1006	                        f"append record {event_id!r}: at does not match event"
1007	                    )
1008	                if change_map[event_id] != recorded_changes:
1009	                    raise ValueError(
1010	                        f"append record {event_id!r}: changes do not match event"
1011	                    )
1012	                if len(parent_map[event_id]) != 1:
1013	                    raise ValueError(
1014	                        f"append record {event_id!r}: event must have exactly "
1015	                        "one parent"
1016	                    )
1017	        merge_by_target: dict[str, list[str]] = {name: [] for name in heads}
1018	        for event_id, (target, source, recorded_at, recorded_changes) in (
1019	            merges.items()
1020	        ):
1021	            if event_id not in at_values:
1022	                raise ValueError(
1023	                    f"merge record {event_id!r} has no matching event"
1024	                )
1025	            if at_values[event_id] != recorded_at:
1026	                raise ValueError(
1027	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: at does not match event"
1028	                )
1029	            if change_map[event_id] != recorded_changes:
1030	                raise ValueError(
1031	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: changes do not match event"
1032	                )
1033	            event_parents = parent_map[event_id]
1034	            if len(event_parents) != 2:
1035	                raise ValueError(
1036	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: event must have exactly "
1037	                    "two parents"
1038	                )
1039	            merge_by_target[target].append(event_id)
1040	
1041	        def ancestors(head: str) -> set[str]:
1042	            closure = {head}
1043	            pending = [head]
1044	            while pending:
1045	                current = pending.pop()
1046	                for parent in parent_map[current]:
1047	                    if parent not in closure:
1048	                        closure.add(parent)
1049	                        pending.append(parent)
1050	            return closure
1051	
1052	        # Branch lineage: source -> appends and inbound merges -> head forms
1053	        # one linear chain, consuming every record attributed to the branch.
1054	        chain_events: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
1055	        for name in heads:
1056	            source = sources[name]
1057	            if source not in at_values:
1058	                raise ValueError(
1059	                    f"branch {name!r}: unknown source event {source!r}"
1060	                )
1061	            head = heads[name]
1062	            if head not in at_values:
1063	                raise ValueError(
1064	                    f"branch {name!r}: unknown head event {head!r}"
1065	                )
1066	
1067	            advances = dict(appends.get(name, {}))
1068	            for event_id in merge_by_target[name]:
1069	                advances[event_id] = True
1070	            # first-parent -> advancing event; the linear head chain allows
1071	            # at most one such successor per event.
1072	            successors: dict[str, str] = {}
1073	            for event_id in advances:
1074	                first_parent = parent_map[event_id][0]
1075	                if first_parent in successors:
1076	                    raise ValueError(
1077	                        f"branch {name!r}: events {successors[first_parent]!r} "
1078	                        f"and {event_id!r} both advance head {first_parent!r}"
1079	                    )
1080	                successors[first_parent] = event_id
1081	
1082	            chain: list[str] = []
1083	            current = source
1084	            remaining = set(advances)
1085	            while current != head:
1086	                nxt = successors.get(current)
1087	                if nxt is None:
1088	                    raise ValueError(
1089	                        f"branch {name!r}: head {head!r} is not reachable "
1090	                        f"from source {source!r} through its records"
1091	                    )
1092	                chain.append(nxt)
1093	                remaining.remove(nxt)
1094	                current = nxt
1095	            if remaining:
1096	                raise ValueError(
1097	                    f"branch {name!r}: records "
1098	                    f"{sorted(remaining)} are not on its source-to-head chain"
1099	                )
1100	            chain_events[name] = chain
1101	
1102	        # Merge source parents: (target_head, source_head) order. The source
1103	        # parent must be the last point of the source branch's chain present
1104	        # in the merge event's ancestor closure.
1105	        for event_id, (target, source, _, _) in merges.items():
1106	            target_parent, source_parent = parent_map[event_id]
1107	
1108	            # Reproduce merge()'s conflict check at the recorded heads: the
1109	            # exclusive closures may not touch overlapping change keys.
1110	            target_closure = ancestors(target_parent)
1111	            source_closure = ancestors(source_parent)
1112	            shared = target_closure & source_closure
1113	            target_keys: set[str] = set()
1114	            for exclusive in target_closure - shared:
1115	                target_keys.update(change_map[exclusive])
1116	            source_keys: set[str] = set()
1117	            for exclusive in source_closure - shared:
1118	                source_keys.update(change_map[exclusive])
1119	            overlapping = target_keys & source_keys
1120	            if overlapping:
1121	                raise ValueError(
1122	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: conflicting changes on keys: "
1123	                    + ", ".join(sorted(overlapping))
1124	                )
1125	
1126	            source_chain = [sources[source]] + chain_events[source]
1127	            if source_parent not in source_chain:
1128	                raise ValueError(
1129	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: source parent "
1130	                    f"{source_parent!r} is not on branch {source!r}'s chain"
1131	                )
1132	            position = source_chain.index(source_parent)
1133	            if position + 1 < len(source_chain):
1134	                later = source_chain[position + 1]
1135	                if later in ancestors(event_id):
1136	                    raise ValueError(
1137	                        f"merge record {event_id!r}: source branch "
1138	                        f"{source!r} had advanced past {source_parent!r} "
1139	                        "before the merge"
1140	                    )
1141	            # Target-side agreement is implied by the target chain walk, but
1142	            # assert the recorded first parent actually precedes the merge.
1143	            target_chain = [sources[target]] + chain_events[target]
1144	            if event_id not in target_chain:
1145	                raise ValueError(
1146	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: not on target branch "
1147	                    f"{target!r}'s chain"
1148	                )
1149	            target_position = target_chain.index(event_id)
1150	            if target_chain[target_position - 1] != target_parent:
1151	                raise ValueError(
1152	                    f"merge record {event_id!r}: first parent does not match "
1153	                    f"target branch {target!r}'s head"
1154	                )

1156	    def audit_merge(self, id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
1157	        """Return an audit record for the merge event ``id``.
1158	
1159	        The record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
1160	        ``event_id, target, source, parents, at, changes``: the merge
1161	        event id, the target and source branch names, the recorded
1162	        parent ids (target head first), the non-negative timestamp and
1163	        a copy of the merged changes. Unknown ids and ids of non-merge

1165	        its ``changes`` never affects the store's records.

1172	        return {
1173	            "event_id": id,
1174	            "target": target,
1175	            "source": source,
1176	            "parents": self._graph._parents[id],
1177	            "at": at_value,
1178	            "changes": dict(changes),

1181	    def audit_log(self) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
1182	        """Return audit records for every event this store recorded.
1183	
1184	        Covers exactly the branch appends and merges performed through
1185	        this store -- events added directly to the graph are not
1186	        included -- each exactly once, ordered by ``(at, event_id)``
1187	        ascending (event ids compared by Unicode code point). Each
1188	        record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
1189	        ``event_id, kind, owner, peer, parents, at, changes``: for an
1190	        append, ``owner`` is the branch name, ``peer`` is ``None`` and
1191	        ``parents`` is the single-element parent id tuple; for a merge,
1192	        ``owner`` is the target branch, ``peer`` is the source branch
1193	        and ``parents`` is the two-element tuple with the target parent
1194	        first. ``changes`` is a copy ordered by Unicode code point of
1195	        its keys. The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and
1196	        records are never modified, and the returned tuple, dicts and
1197	        changes are detached from internal state, so mutating them
1198	        affects neither the store nor later calls, and repeated calls
1199	        return item-wise equal results in a stable order.
1200	        """
1201	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1202	        for name, appends in self._appends.items():
1203	            for event_id, (at_value, changes) in appends.items():
